checks.name: FINDING 2 (PREDICTION FALSIFIED): the split terms are NOT single-mode
checks.detail: PREDICTED, from sum c^2 being a single Kerov mode (m = 3): each half of the split is single-mode too, so |rho| -> 1 for both and the cancellation becomes a ratio of two constants. FALSE. rho(sum|c_k|, sum c^2) = ['0.979439', '0.980211', '0.980236', '0.978658', '0.978852'] -- FLAT, total spread 0.00158 over a 16x range in n, and nowhere near 1. rho(sum D_k, sum c^2) = ['-0.937145', '-0.94554', '-0.94927', '-0.946774', '-0.948421']. Yet the combination reaches rho(sum h, sum c^2) = ['0.974449', '0.985128', '0.992036', '0.995488', '0.997519']. So the OFF-MODE parts of sum|c_k| and 2 sum D_k cancel each other: sum h is nearly a pure m = 3 statistic while neither of its parts is. That is why the cancellation does not reduce to two constants -- and a sharper account of why sum h is the special combination than 'it is conjugation-symmetric'.
